s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in a patient with multiple ocular and systemic comorbidities
salient_findings: Blurry vision in the left eye for 6 days
Best-corrected visual acuity of count fingers at 2 ft in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye
Bilateral optic nerve head pallor and 360° photocoagulation scars
Intraretinal and subretinal fluid in the fovea on optical coherence tomography
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
History of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis
Treated with siponimod for 5 months
Type 2 diabetes mellitus complicated by proliferative diabetic retinopathy
Treated with pan-retinal photocoagulation
Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome
Chronic renal failure
Blurry vision in the left eye for 6 days
Best-corrected visual acuity of count fingers at 2 ft in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure was 16 mm Hg bilaterally
Moderate nuclear sclerotic cataracts
Bilateral optic nerve head pallor (cup-to-disc ratio 0.3)
360° photocoagulation scars
No prior history of macular oedema
Hemoglobin A1c one month earlier was 10.2%
Optical coherence tomography of the left eye revealed intraretinal and subretinal fluid in the fovea
Repeat OCT demonstrated worsening bilateral cystoid macular oedema
Intravenous fluorescein angiography revealed late petaloid macular leakage and late optic disc staining

shortlist.label: Diabetic Macular Edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus and optical coherence tomography revealed intraretinal and subretinal fluid in the fovea

shortlist.label: Cystoid Macular Edema
shortlist.why_kept: Repeat OCT demonstrated worsening bilateral cystoid macular oedema

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis-associated Optic Neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and presented with blurry vision

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome-related Retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has antiphospholipid antibody syndrome and presented with vision loss

shortlist.label: Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus complicated by proliferative diabetic retinopathy

raw.rationale: The presence of intraretinal and subretinal fluid in the fovea on optical coherence tomography and late petaloid macular leakage on intravenous fluorescein angiography are characteristic of cystoid macular edema, which is further supported by the worsening bilateral cystoid macular oedema on repeat OCT.

rejected.label: Diabetic Macular Edema
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and proliferative diabetic retinopathy, the absence of prior macular oedema and the specific findings on OCT and fluorescein angiography point more towards cystoid macular edema as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis-associated Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: The patient's history of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and treatment with siponimod could suggest optic neuritis, but the key findings of intraretinal and subretinal fluid and late petaloid macular leakage are more indicative of cystoid macular edema.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome-related Retinopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, the specific ocular findings presented are more characteristic of cystoid macular edema than the retinopathy associated with antiphospholipid syndrome.

rejected.label: Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy
rejected.why: The patient's history of proliferative diabetic retinopathy is noted, but the current presentation of blurry vision and the findings on OCT and fluorescein angiography are more directly related to cystoid macular edema.
